message: Select a Swamp or Mountain card
annotation_description: Fetching Raucous Theater (enters tapped) instead of Blood Crypt (can enter untapped for 2 life) means they cannot cast any spells on turn 1 despite having Faithless Looting and Thoughtseize in hand. Turn 1 Thoughtseize is extremely valuable for disruption, and Faithless Looting would advance their graveyard plan.

Discarding Island when only having 1 land on the battlefield and desperately needing to make land drops. With two copies of the legendary Gran-Gran in hand (only one can be on the battlefield at a time), discarding a duplicate legendary is better than discarding a land when severely mana-starved.

message: Put a permanent card into your hand?
annotation_description: With Sire of Seven Deaths (7 mana, colorless Eldrazi) and Emrakul in hand, Ugin's Labyrinth would have been significantly better. Ugin's Labyrinth can imprint a colorless card with mana value 7+ (like Sire of Seven Deaths or Emrakul) to produce 2 colorless mana per tap, effectively acting as a Sol land. The player already has multiple colorless Eldrazi to imprint. Eldrazi Temple only produces 2 colorless mana specifically for Eldrazi spells/abilities, while Ugin's Labyrinth does the same with imprint but is a land that can be played immediately and doesn't have the Eldrazi-only restriction on the bonus mana. More importantly, the player put TWO copies of Ugin's Labyrinth into the graveyard by not picking one, losing access to both. With Icetill Explorer in hand (which lets you play lands from graveyard), one copy could potentially be recovered, but having it in hand is still better. Ugin's Labyrinth with imprint would have provided faster acceleration toward casting Emrakul or Sire.

Took Sire of Seven Deaths instead of Emrakul, the Promised End with Thoughtseize. Emrakul's cast trigger (controlling opponent's next turn) is essentially game-ending, and taking Sire puts a creature card type in the graveyard, reducing Emrakul's cost from 9 to 8. The opponent has Icetill Explorer enabling land replay from graveyard (including 2x Ugin's Labyrinth which can imprint Emrakul for massive mana), making casting Emrakul very realistic.

GLM47 Coach passed the turn with 3 mana available (Steam Vents + Polluted Delta for a land) and multiple playable cards. Gran-Gran costs {U} and could have been cast off Steam Vents, providing a body that loots when tapped and potentially enables cost reduction later. The opponent has an Icetill Explorer (2/4) that is generating value through land-from-graveyard and mill, and a Sire of Seven Deaths in the graveyard that could be reanimated or recast. Developing the board with Gran-Gran would help find answers and apply pressure. Additionally, Faithless Looting could have been cast to improve hand quality and stock the graveyard for Persist (which could target the opponent's Sire of Seven Deaths from their graveyard - though Persist only works on your own graveyard). At minimum, casting Gran-Gran for {U} to develop the board was free and had no downside.

Casting Emperor of Bones before combat is suboptimal sequencing. Emperor of Bones has an 'at the beginning of combat on your turn' trigger that exiles a card from a graveyard, which won't trigger this turn since the precombat main phase hasn't moved to combat yet — wait, actually the combat trigger will still happen this turn since it triggers at the beginning of combat. However, casting a creature before combat when holding Fatal Push and Bitter Triumph (trick-style cards) gives the opponent information unnecessarily. More importantly, the player should consider sequencing: they have Polluted Delta uncracked, and should likely crack it first to enable Revolt for Fatal Push (which could kill Icetill Explorer, a 2/4 with mana value 4). Playing Emperor of Bones before cracking Polluted Delta means if they need Fatal Push with Revolt later this turn, they've used mana on the creature first. Additionally, Faithless Looting could be cast first to improve hand quality and potentially set up better plays, since Emperor of Bones wants good targets in graveyards to reanimate.

Should play a land from graveyard first (via Icetill Explorer) before casting Sowing Mycospawn. Playing Eldrazi Temple from graveyard would add extra mana and trigger landfall/mill, potentially enabling additional plays this turn (like also casting Talisman of Impulse). Land drops should come before spell casting for maximum mana efficiency.

Casting Bitter Triumph in response to their own Faithless Looting means they must discard a card (or pay 3 life) before seeing the 2 cards Faithless Looting would draw. By letting Looting resolve first, they'd have 2 additional cards to choose from as discard fodder for both Bitter Triumph and Looting's discard, maximizing card selection.

Discarded Psychic Frog (a premier win condition and card advantage engine) instead of one of the two duplicate Gran-Grans in hand. Gran-Gran without Lessons in graveyard is just a 1/2 looter, and having two copies makes one very expendable. Psychic Frog is significantly more impactful as a threat that can grow, gain flying, and draw cards.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Discarding Fatal Push over a second copy of Gran-Gran is debatable. Fatal Push is premium removal that could deal with future threats, while having two Gran-Gran in hand is redundant (legendary creature). Against an Eldrazi ramp deck, Fatal Push may not line up perfectly with their biggest threats, but it still has value against Sowing Mycospawn (MV 4 with revolt) or other mid-sized creatures.

message: Select up to one card from a graveyard
annotation_description: Exiled Psychic Frog (1/2) with Emperor of Bones instead of Devourer of Destiny (6/6) from opponent's graveyard. When Emperor of Bones adapts and reanimates the exiled creature, a 6/6 hasty attacker is far more impactful than a 1/2 Psychic Frog (which would need hand cards discarded to pump and gets sacrificed at end step regardless). This also has the secondary benefit of denying the opponent a powerful card from their graveyard.

Sonnet Gramps had enough mana to cast Sowing Mycospawn with kicker but chose to cast it unkicked. With Forest+Utopia Sprawl (GG), Forest (G), Stomping Ground (G/R), Eldrazi Temple (CC for colorless Eldrazi), and Eldrazi Spawn (C), they had at least 7 mana available, more than enough for the kicked cost of {3}{G}{1}{C} (6 total). Kicking it would exile one of the opponent's three lands, which would be devastating against an opponent at only 3 lands with Emperor of Bones as their only threat.

Bojuka Bog enters tapped, preventing Emrakul from being cast this turn. With 5 card types in graveyard (land, instant/kindred, sorcery, artifact, creature), Emrakul costs 8. Current mana production is 7 (Forest+Sprawl=2, Forest=1, Stomping Ground=1, Eldrazi Temple=2 for Eldrazi, Spawn=1). Playing Verdant Catacombs (fetching untapped) or Sanctum of Ugin would provide the 8th mana needed to cast Emrakul this turn, gaining control of the opponent's next turn.

Chose to reanimate Psychic Frog (1/2) instead of Sire of Seven Deaths (7/7 with first strike, menace, trample, lifelink, haste). Sire would have been nearly unblockable with menace (opponent only has Sowing Mycospawn and an Eldrazi Spawn token), would deal significant trample damage, and gain 7 life with lifelink. The creature gets sacrificed at end of turn regardless, so maximum immediate impact is what matters.

Discarded a land (Undercity Sewers) when at only 3 lands on board, rather than discarding one of two copies of the legendary Gran-Gran. With only 3 lands, the 4th land drop is important for deploying threats and casting spells. Since Gran-Gran is legendary, the second copy has significantly reduced value.

Gran-Gran has 'Whenever Gran-Gran becomes tapped, draw a card, then discard a card.' Attacking with Gran-Gran provides a free loot trigger. The opponent's only meaningful blocker is Sowing Mycospawn (3/3), which they're unlikely to use on a 1/2. The Eldrazi Spawn (0/1) could chump but that's a fine trade. The player also has a duplicate Gran-Gran in hand, reducing the risk of losing it.

Sonnet Gramps chose not to block Emperor of Bones (4/4) with the Eldrazi Spawn Token (0/1), which would have absorbed no damage but could have chumped to save 4 life. At 17 life going to 13, this matters because the opponent has an aggressive deck. The Eldrazi Spawn token provides {C} when sacrificed, but with Emrakul in hand and a developing board, saving 4 life by chump blocking with a 0/1 token that provides only 1 colorless mana seems like the better trade. The mana from the spawn is relatively minor compared to 4 life points.

Gran-Gran is a legendary creature, and GLM47 Coach already has a Gran-Gran on the battlefield. Casting a second Gran-Gran will cause the legend rule to apply, forcing the player to sacrifice one of the two copies. This wastes a card for essentially no benefit - at best, they get a single loot trigger from the new Gran-Gran becoming tapped (but it was just cast, so it won't tap unless they have a way to tap it). Meanwhile, they have Psychic Frog available to cast, which would be a much more impactful play as a 1/2 that can grow, gain flying, and draw cards on combat damage.

Discarded Persist instead of the duplicate legendary Gran-Gran. The second Gran-Gran cannot be cast while the first is on the battlefield (legend rule would immediately kill one). Persist at least has future potential if creatures die - Emperor of Bones or Psychic Frog could become valid targets later.

Not attacking with Gran-Gran means missing a free loot trigger (draw + discard) since Gran-Gran draws a card when it becomes tapped. With 0 cards in hand, this card filtering is very valuable. Psychic Frog could also potentially sneak in for damage and a card draw if unblocked.

At 9 life against a board with Psychic Frog (which can pump and gain flying), declining to block Emperor of Bones drops to 5 life, putting them in lethal range. The Eldrazi Spawn token could chump block to save 4 life at minimal cost (sacrificing a 0/1 token), though preserving it for Emrakul mana is a consideration.

Playing Eldrazi Temple instead of Sanctum of Ugin when both provide enough mana to cast the discounted Emrakul this turn. Sanctum of Ugin would trigger on casting Emrakul (colorless spell with MV 7+), allowing a sacrifice to tutor for another colorless creature, providing significant card advantage.

Emrakul, the Promised End costs 7 mana (13 minus 6 card types in graveyard: land, instant, sorcery, artifact, creature, kindred). With Forest+Utopia Sprawl (2), Forest (1), Eldrazi Temple (2 for Eldrazi), Stomping Ground (1), Bojuka Bog (1), and Eldrazi Spawn sacrifice (1) = 8 mana available, Emrakul could be cast this turn while the opponent is completely tapped out. Emrakul's mind control trigger plus a 13/13 flying trampler would likely win the game.

message: Select up to one card from a graveyard
annotation_description: Exiled Persist (a sorcery) with Emperor of Bones instead of Abhorrent Oculus (a 5/5 flying creature). Emperor of Bones can only reanimate creature cards exiled with it, so exiling Persist accomplishes nothing. With Abhorrent Oculus exiled, they could adapt Emperor of Bones for {1}{B} (mana available from untapped lands), putting a 4/4 flying Oculus onto the battlefield with haste. Combined with potentially pumping Psychic Frog by discarding the Psychic Frog from hand, they could attack for significant flying damage against an opponent at 9 life. Instead they skipped attacks entirely.

At 9 life facing Emperor of Bones, Gran-Gran, and Psychic Frog, casting Talisman of Impulse for ramp is lower priority than addressing the board. Additionally, land should be played before casting spells - Sanctum of Ugin is particularly valuable as it synergizes with casting Emrakul later. Kozilek's Return would clear all three opposing creatures (all have 2 or less toughness) and set up the graveyard trigger for later Emrakul cast.

message: Select up to one card from a graveyard
annotation_description: Emperor of Bones can only reanimate creature cards exiled with it when it gets +1/+1 counters via Adapt. Exiling Malevolent Rumble (a sorcery) means Emperor of Bones cannot reanimate anything. Abhorrent Oculus (5/5 flyer) was available in their own graveyard and could have been exiled, then reanimated with haste by paying {1}{B} for Adapt 2. With opponent at 9 life, a 5/5 flying haste attacker alongside existing creatures could threaten lethal.

Attacking Emperor of Bones into Sowing Mycospawn (3/3) risks losing a valuable creature that provides graveyard interaction and reanimation. Opponent is at 9 life, so 4 total damage isn't close to lethal, and losing Emperor of Bones to a bad trade weakens the board significantly.

Kozilek's Return would deal 2 damage to all creatures, killing Emperor of Bones (2/2), Gran-Gran (1/2), and possibly Psychic Frog, while keeping Sowing Mycospawn (3/3) alive. Additionally, putting Kozilek's Return in the graveyard sets up its powerful second ability with Emrakul, the Promised End in hand - when Emrakul is cast, Kozilek's Return can be exiled from graveyard to deal 5 damage to all creatures.

message: Select up to one card from a graveyard (as <font color='#20B2AA'>GLM47 Coach</font>)
annotation_description: Sonnet Gramps is at 3 life with only Sowing Mycospawn (3/3) to block. GLM47 Coach has Psychic Frog (1/2), Emperor of Bones (2/2), and Gran-Gran (1/2). By discarding one card to pump Psychic Frog to 2/3, then attacking with all three (2+2+1=5 power), Sonnet Gramps can only block one creature. Blocking either 2-power creature lets 2+1=3 through for lethal. Even without pump, if opponent blocks the 2/2, only 2 gets through, but with the pump making two 2-power threats, any single block lets exactly 3 through.

message: Play spells and abilities (as <font color='#20B2AA'>GLM47 Coach</font>)
annotation_description: While controlling the opponent's turn via Emrakul, Sonnet Gramps passed without using Psychic Frog's activated ability to exile 3 cards from the opponent's graveyard (which included Abhorrent Oculus, Gran-Gran, Emperor of Bones). Exiling these cards would strip the opponent of powerful reanimation targets and future graveyard synergies at no real cost.

message: Play instants and activated abilities (as <font color='#20B2AA'>GLM47 Coach</font>)
annotation_description: During the Emrakul control turn's end step, the player passed without activating any of GLM47 Coach's abilities. Gran-Gran could be tapped to draw/discard (letting the controller choose what to discard), and Psychic Frog could discard cards from their hand to waste resources. These activations would strip the opponent's hand of valuable cards before they get their extra turn.

message: Select a creature card with mana value 3 or less from your graveyard
annotation_description: Opponent is at 3 life. Abhorrent Oculus (mana value 3) is a legal Unearth target and would enter as a 5/5 flyer - since Unearth puts it onto the battlefield without casting, the 'exile six cards' additional cost doesn't apply. A 5/5 flyer is lethal on its own against an opponent at 3 life with no flying blockers. Instead, Gran-Gran (1/2) was chosen, which provides minimal board impact.

message: Select up to one card from a graveyard
annotation_description: Opponent is at 3 life with only Sowing Mycospawn (3/3) as a blocker. By discarding an Archon of Cruelty to Psychic Frog to make it 2/3, then attacking with all three creatures (Emperor 2/2, Frog 2/3, Gran-Gran 1/2), no matter which creature the opponent blocks with Mycospawn, the remaining two deal at least 3 damage, which is lethal.

message: Select up to one card from a graveyard
annotation_description: Opponent is at 3 life with no creatures on the battlefield. Emperor of Bones (2/2) can Adapt 2 for {1}{B} to become 4/4, and Gran-Gran is a 1/2. Attacking with both deals 5 damage to an empty board, which is lethal against an opponent at 3 life. Instead, the attack was skipped entirely.

Kozilek's Return deals 2 damage to EACH CREATURE, not to opponents. It's a board wipe effect, not a burn spell. The player is at 3 life and the opponent is at 2 life, but Kozilek's Return cannot deal damage to players. Casting it kills the opponent's Emperor of Bones and Gran-Gran, but also means Sonnet Gramps paid 1 life from Talisman of Impulse to tap for red mana, going to 2 life themselves. Meanwhile, the opponent at 2 life has no way to be killed by this spell. The player should have looked for an actual way to deal 2 damage to the opponent, or focused on setting up a board state to attack for lethal. With 7 lands in play plus Talisman, they could cast Sowing Mycospawn (which is a creature that could attack next turn) while also developing their board. The Kozilek's Return accomplishes clearing the opponent's creatures but doesn't win the game as the player's reasoning incorrectly assumed.

The reasoning for casting Kozilek's Return is fundamentally wrong - it deals damage to creatures only, not players, so it cannot 'finish them off' at 2 life. While killing Emperor of Bones is useful, the player should have played a land first (Forest from hand) before casting spells, following proper sequencing. The misunderstanding of the card suggests the player may have cast it primarily for the wrong reason, though it does have board value.
